# pai pane

Run a command in a visible pane: run

```
pai pane <command>
```

Everything a session starts that does not run in its own pane runs in one: `pai pane run` is the way for background commands. See docs/worker-panes.md.

```sh
pai pane run --label tests -- npx vitest run
pai pane run -- sleep 30
```

See also: `pai worker run`, `pai build run`

### pai pane run

Run a command in a visible pane and wait for it

```
pai pane run [options]
```

Opens one pane (split of this window, never a new window) FIRST and runs the command in it as the child of `pai pane exec`, which shows the live output and its exit code, writes <PAI home>/state/pane-exec/<id>.exit and closes the pane when the command ends, whatever the exit code. The caller tees the output to <PAI home>/logs/panes/<id>.log and blocks until the command ends. With no terminal at all the command is refused (no pane: REASON) unless workers.panes.required is false. Then it prints the last 40 lines and exits with the command's exit code, so a backgrounded call still reports back to the session. SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP to this command kill the command's whole process group. Every background shell command of a session goes through here: the Bash guard denies a bare run_in_background command. Several words are exec'd as given; a single word is run by sh -c.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--label TEXT` | string | — | Name shown in `pai worker ps` and the cockpit (default: the command) |
| `--cwd DIR` | string | — | Directory to run in (default: here) |

```sh
pai pane run --label tests -- npx vitest run
pai pane run --cwd ~/proj -- make build
pai pane run -- sleep 30
```

See also: `pai worker ps`, `pai worker follow`, `pai build run`

### pai pane exec

Internal: the wrapper a pane runs; owns the process started in it

```
pai pane exec ID
```

The command of every pane PAI opens for a process it starts (a worker, a plan runner, `pai pane run`). It connects to the starting `pai` process, which sends the real command; the wrapper runs it as its child, shows its output in the pane, writes <PAI home>/state/pane-exec/<id>.exit (exit code + end time) and exits when the child exits, so the pane closes with the process. If the starting process goes away, the child is killed. Not for direct use.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ID` | yes | Run id the starting process listens for |

```sh
pai pane exec pane-20260101-0000-ab12
```

See also: `pai pane run`

### pai pane close-finished

Close every pane whose process has ended

```
pai pane close-finished [options]
```

Closes each registered pane whose owned process is gone and whose linger has run out (8 s, clean or failed; panes.exitLingerSecs). A pane with a live process is never closed. The daemon does the same every 30 s; a failure stays readable with `pai worker replay <id>`.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | flag | — | Only list what would be closed |

```sh
pai pane close-finished
pai pane close-finished --dry-run
```

See also: `pai worker replay`, `pai worker ps --panes`
